title: A golden age of science is coming
gist: Noah Smith argues AI is reversing the long scientific slowdown ('ideas getting harder to find') by removing the cap on effective researchers, collapsing the theory bottleneck, and making literature review instant and cross-disciplinary. He cites early results from Anthropic, OpenAI's GPT-Rosalind and Google's Gemini 4 Argon, and speculates AI may discover 'cloud laws' humans cannot grasp, provided it gets massive sensor data.

insights.claim: Before AI, prominent research such as 'Are Ideas Getting Harder to Find?' suggested science was in terminal decline, requiring ever more researchers just to sustain a fraction of past progress.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: The pre-AI baseline was declining research productivity, which is what AI may now reverse.
insights.quote: It looked like science was hitting a wall. Then along came AI.
insights.locator: It’s almost hard to remember

insights.claim: Smith predicts the next few decades will be an amazing time for science, though AI may eventually run into diminishing returns.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: A long-duration productivity tailwind thesis supportive of AI and science-heavy sectors.
insights.quote: the next few decades are probably going to be an absolutely amazing time for human science
insights.locator: But as cool as these stories sound

insights.claim: It is too early to tell how much AI will speed up total factor productivity growth, but signs of a scientific speedup are already visible.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: Macro productivity effects remain unproven even if science-level signals are positive.
insights.quote: It’s far too early to tell how much AI will eventually speed up the growth of total factor productivity.

insights.claim: Smith predicts AI will essentially eliminate the theory bottleneck in science, or at least cut the turnaround between experiment and theory by an order of magnitude.

insights.so_what: Faster theory-experiment loops accelerate R&D cycles in physics, materials and biology.

insights.claim: An OpenAI model recently solved major open problems in computer science, math and theoretical physics, including a proof that the Standard Model of particle physics can be mathematically well-defined.

insights.locator: AI is an absolute beast at math.

insights.claim: Historical examples show theory lags experiment: Planck took a couple of years to explain blackbody radiation and Watson and Crick about a year to find DNA's structure after the data existed.
